usageNotes: Use this to open an interactive console session to a running LXC container via VNC; the response returns a short-lived ticket, one-time password, port, and TLS cert needed to connect a VNC client or Proxmox's noVNC web console. The caller must hold the VM.Console privilege on /vms/{vmid} and the container's node must be online. Enable the 'websocket' flag when connecting through Proxmox's built-in web UI (noVNC); omit it for raw TCP VNC clients.

examples.summary: Open a websocket VNC proxy session for LXC 200 on node pve1 at 1280×720

tips: The returned ticket and password are single-use and expire quickly; connect immediately after receiving the response.
The 'port' in the response is ephemeral and allocated on the target node — ensure your client can reach that node's port directly, not just the API host.
Width and height only hint the initial console geometry; the container's getty or init system controls the actual terminal size independently.
If the container is stopped, this call will fail — check container status with get_nodes_node_lxc_vmid_status_current before calling.
